q: What does Amazon EC2 stand for?

exp.a: Incorrect – The correct term uses 'Compute Cloud', not 'Cloud Computing'.
exp.b: Correct – EC2 stands for Elastic Compute Cloud, a web service that provides resizable compute capacity in the cloud.
exp.c: Incorrect – 'Electronic' is not part of the EC2 full form.
exp.d: Incorrect – EC2 is not a cluster; it stands for Elastic Compute Cloud.

q: Which of the following is the default maximum number of EC2 instances you can launch per region in a new AWS account (On-Demand)?

exp.a: Incorrect – 5 is the default limit for Elastic IPs, not EC2 instances.
exp.b: Correct – The default On-Demand instance limit per region is 20 (for most instance families). You can request an increase.
exp.c: Incorrect – 50 is not the default limit for On-Demand EC2 instances.
exp.d: Incorrect – 100 exceeds the default limit for new accounts.

q: What is the default number of Elastic IP addresses allowed per AWS account per region?

exp.a: Incorrect – The default is 5, not 3.
exp.b: Correct – AWS allows 5 Elastic IP addresses per region per account by default.
exp.c: Incorrect – 10 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: Incorrect – 15 exceeds the default limit.

q: Which EC2 pricing model offers the highest discount (up to 90%) compared to On-Demand pricing?

exp.a: Incorrect – Reserved Instances offer up to 72% discount, not 90%.
exp.b: Correct – Spot Instances can offer up to 90% discount compared to On-Demand pricing, but can be interrupted.
exp.c: Incorrect – Dedicated Hosts do not offer the highest discount.
exp.d: Incorrect – Savings Plans offer up to 72% discount, not 90%.

q: What is the maximum discount offered by Reserved Instances compared to On-Demand pricing?

exp.a: Incorrect – Reserved Instances can offer more than 50% discount.
exp.b: Incorrect – The maximum is higher than 60%.
exp.c: Correct – Reserved Instances offer up to 72% discount compared to On-Demand pricing.
exp.d: Incorrect – 90% discount is associated with Spot Instances, not Reserved Instances.

q: Which EC2 instance type is best suited for memory-intensive applications like in-memory databases?

exp.a: Incorrect – C-series is optimized for compute-intensive tasks, not memory.
exp.b: Correct – R-series instances are memory optimized and ideal for in-memory databases like Redis, SAP HANA.
exp.c: Incorrect – T-series is general purpose with burstable performance.
exp.d: Incorrect – I-series is storage optimized for high sequential read/write access.

q: What is the maximum duration for a Spot Instance interruption notice before AWS reclaims the instance?

exp.a: Incorrect – AWS provides more than 30 seconds notice.
exp.b: Incorrect – The notice period is 2 minutes, not 1 minute.
exp.c: Correct – AWS provides a 2-minute interruption notice before terminating a Spot Instance.
exp.d: Incorrect – The notice is 2 minutes, not 5 minutes.

q: Which of the following is NOT a valid EC2 instance state?

exp.a: Incorrect – Running is a valid EC2 instance state.
exp.b: Incorrect – Stopped is a valid EC2 instance state.
exp.c: Correct – 'Paused' is not a valid EC2 instance state. Valid states are: pending, running, stopping, stopped, shutting-down, terminated.
exp.d: Incorrect – Terminated is a valid EC2 instance state.

q: What is the default termination protection setting for a new EC2 instance?

exp.a: Incorrect – Termination protection is disabled by default.
exp.b: Correct – By default, termination protection is disabled. You must manually enable it.
exp.c: Incorrect – It does not depend on instance type; it is always disabled by default.
exp.d: Incorrect – It does not vary by region.

q: Which storage option is ephemeral and loses data when the EC2 instance is stopped or terminated?

exp.a: Incorrect – EBS is persistent storage that retains data even after the instance is stopped.
exp.b: Correct – Instance Store (ephemeral storage) is physically attached to the host and data is lost when the instance stops or terminates.
exp.c: Incorrect – EFS is a managed file system that persists independently.
exp.d: Incorrect – S3 is an object storage service and is persistent.

q: What is the maximum size of a single EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect – EBS volumes can be much larger than 1 TiB.
exp.b: Incorrect – 8 TiB is not the maximum.
exp.c: Correct – The maximum size of a single EBS volume is 16 TiB.
exp.d: Incorrect – 64 TiB exceeds the maximum EBS volume size.

q: Which EBS volume type provides the highest IOPS performance (up to 256,000 IOPS)?

exp.a: Incorrect – gp3 supports up to 16,000 IOPS.
exp.b: Correct – io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS, designed for the most demanding workloads.
exp.c: Incorrect – st1 is HDD-based and optimized for throughput, not IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect – sc1 is designed for infrequent access and has the lowest performance.

q: What is the maximum IOPS supported by a gp3 EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect – 3,000 is the baseline IOPS for gp3, not the maximum.
exp.b: Incorrect – 10,000 is not the max for gp3.
exp.c: Correct – gp3 volumes support up to 16,000 IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect – 64,000 IOPS is the maximum for io2 (non-Block Express).

q: What is the baseline IOPS provided by a gp3 EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect – The baseline is 3,000 IOPS.
exp.b: Correct – gp3 provides a baseline of 3,000 IOPS regardless of volume size.
exp.c: Incorrect – 5,000 is not the baseline.
exp.d: Incorrect – 10,000 exceeds the baseline.

q: Which of the following is used to securely connect to an EC2 instance via SSH?

exp.a: Incorrect – Security Groups control inbound/outbound traffic rules, not authentication.
exp.b: Correct – Key Pairs (public/private keys) are used for SSH authentication to EC2 instances.
exp.c: Incorrect – IAM Roles grant permissions to AWS services, not SSH access.
exp.d: Incorrect – NACLs control traffic at subnet level, not authentication.

q: What port number is used for SSH access to a Linux EC2 instance?

exp.a: Correct – Port 22 is the default port for SSH (Secure Shell) connections.
exp.b: Incorrect – Port 80 is for HTTP traffic.
exp.c: Incorrect – Port 443 is for HTTPS traffic.
exp.d: Incorrect – Port 3389 is for RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) used with Windows instances.

q: What port number is used for RDP access to a Windows EC2 instance?

exp.a: Incorrect – Port 22 is for SSH (Linux).
exp.b: Incorrect – Port 80 is for HTTP.
exp.c: Incorrect – Port 443 is for HTTPS.
exp.d: Correct – Port 3389 is used for Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) to connect to Windows EC2 instances.

q: Security Groups in AWS are:

exp.a: Incorrect – NACLs are stateless, not Security Groups.
exp.b: Correct – Security Groups are stateful, meaning if you allow inbound traffic, the response is automatically allowed outbound.
exp.c: Incorrect – Security Groups are only stateful.
exp.d: Incorrect – Security Groups are stateful.

q: Network ACLs (NACLs) in AWS are:

exp.a: Incorrect – NACLs are stateless; Security Groups are stateful.
exp.b: Correct – NACLs are stateless, meaning both inbound and outbound rules are evaluated independently.
exp.c: Incorrect – NACLs are applied at the subnet level, not instance level.
exp.d: Incorrect – NACLs support both allow and deny rules.

q: What is the default behavior of a Security Group for inbound traffic?

exp.a: Incorrect – By default, all inbound traffic is denied.
exp.b: Correct – By default, a Security Group denies all inbound traffic. You must explicitly add rules to allow traffic.
exp.c: Incorrect – SSH is not allowed by default.
exp.d: Incorrect – HTTP is not allowed by default.

q: What is the default behavior of a Security Group for outbound traffic?

exp.a: Incorrect – By default, all outbound traffic is allowed.
exp.b: Correct – By default, a Security Group allows all outbound traffic.
exp.c: Incorrect – All outbound traffic is allowed, not just port 80.
exp.d: Incorrect – All outbound traffic is allowed, not just port 443.

q: Which EC2 purchasing option requires a commitment of 1 or 3 years?

exp.a: Incorrect – On-Demand has no long-term commitment.
exp.b: Incorrect – Spot Instances have no commitment; they can be interrupted anytime.
exp.c: Correct – Reserved Instances require a 1-year or 3-year term commitment for significant discounts.
exp.d: Incorrect – Dedicated Instances can be On-Demand without a term commitment.

q: What is an AMI in AWS?

exp.a: Correct – AMI stands for Amazon Machine Image, a template used to launch EC2 instances.
exp.b: Incorrect – AMI stands for Amazon Machine Image.
exp.c: Incorrect – AMI is not related to interfaces.
exp.d: Incorrect – AMI is not related to monitoring.

q: Can an AMI be shared across AWS regions?

opts.a: Yes, AMIs are global by default
opts.b: No, AMIs are region-specific but can be copied to other regions
opts.c: No, AMIs cannot be used in other regions at all
opts.d: Yes, but only for public AMIs

exp.a: Incorrect – AMIs are region-specific, not global.
exp.b: Correct – AMIs are region-specific but you can copy them to other regions.
exp.c: Incorrect – You can copy AMIs to other regions.
exp.d: Incorrect – Both public and private AMIs can be copied across regions.

q: What is the purpose of an EC2 Placement Group?

opts.a: To place instances in different AWS accounts
opts.b: To control the placement of instances on underlying hardware
opts.c: To assign Elastic IPs to instances
opts.d: To create backup copies of instances

exp.a: Incorrect – Placement Groups are not for cross-account placement.
exp.b: Correct – Placement Groups control how instances are placed on the underlying hardware for performance or fault tolerance.
exp.c: Incorrect – Elastic IPs are unrelated to Placement Groups.
exp.d: Incorrect – Backups are done using AMIs or snapshots, not Placement Groups.

q: Which EC2 Placement Group strategy places instances across different hardware racks?

exp.a: Incorrect – Cluster places instances close together in a single AZ for low latency.
exp.b: Correct – Spread placement group places each instance on distinct hardware racks to reduce correlated failures.
exp.c: Incorrect – Partition divides instances into logical partitions across racks.
exp.d: Incorrect – 'Default' is not a named placement group strategy.

q: What is the maximum number of instances per Availability Zone in a Spread Placement Group?

exp.a: Incorrect – The limit is 7, not 5.
exp.b: Correct – A Spread Placement Group supports a maximum of 7 running instances per AZ.
exp.c: Incorrect – 10 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect – 15 exceeds the limit.

q: Which service is used to automatically scale EC2 instances based on demand?

exp.a: Incorrect – Lambda is serverless and does not manage EC2 scaling.
exp.b: Correct – EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances based on demand.
exp.c: Incorrect – Elastic Beanstalk is a deployment service that may use Auto Scaling internally.
exp.d: Incorrect – CloudFront is a CDN, not a scaling service.

q: In an Auto Scaling Group, what defines the minimum number of instances that must always be running?

exp.a: Incorrect – Desired Capacity is the number of instances ASG tries to maintain at any time.
exp.b: Incorrect – Maximum Capacity is the upper limit.
exp.c: Correct – Minimum Capacity sets the floor; Auto Scaling will never scale below this number.
exp.d: Incorrect – Scaling Policy defines when to scale, not the minimum.

q: What is the default cooldown period for an Auto Scaling Group?

exp.a: Incorrect – 60 seconds is not the default cooldown.
exp.b: Incorrect – 120 seconds is not the default.
exp.c: Correct – The default cooldown period is 300 seconds (5 minutes).
exp.d: Incorrect – 600 seconds exceeds the default.

q: Which AWS service distributes incoming traffic across multiple EC2 instances?

exp.a: Incorrect – Route 53 is a DNS service, though it can do routing, it's not a load balancer.
exp.b: Correct – ELB distributes incoming application traffic across multiple EC2 instances.
exp.c: Incorrect – CloudTrail is for auditing API calls.
exp.d: Incorrect – VPC is a virtual network, not a load balancer.

q: Which type of Elastic Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS)?

exp.a: Incorrect – NLB operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP).
exp.b: Correct – Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 and supports HTTP/HTTPS routing.
exp.c: Incorrect – Classic Load Balancer supports both Layer 4 and Layer 7 but is legacy.
exp.d: Incorrect – Gateway Load Balancer operates at Layer 3 for third-party appliances.

q: Which type of Elastic Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) and can handle millions of requests per second?

exp.a: Incorrect – ALB operates at Layer 7.
exp.b: Correct – Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and is designed for ultra-high performance and low latency.
exp.c: Incorrect – Classic Load Balancer is legacy and not optimized for extreme throughput.
exp.d: Incorrect – Gateway Load Balancer is for deploying third-party virtual appliances.

q: What is the purpose of an EC2 User Data script?

opts.b: To run commands at instance launch (bootstrapping)

exp.a: Incorrect – User Data is not for encryption.
exp.b: Correct – User Data allows you to run scripts (bash/PowerShell) at instance launch for bootstrapping (installing software, updates, etc.).
exp.c: Incorrect – IAM users are created through IAM, not User Data.
exp.d: Incorrect – Billing alerts are configured in CloudWatch/Budgets.

q: EC2 User Data scripts run with which user privilege by default on Linux?

exp.a: Incorrect – User Data runs as root, not ec2-user.
exp.b: Incorrect – User Data runs as root, not ubuntu.
exp.c: Correct – EC2 User Data scripts execute with root privileges by default.
exp.d: Incorrect – User Data runs as root.

q: What is the maximum size of EC2 User Data?

exp.a: Incorrect – The maximum is 16 KB.
exp.b: Correct – EC2 User Data is limited to 16 KB in size.
exp.c: Incorrect – 64 KB exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect – 128 KB exceeds the limit.

q: Which of the following instance families is optimized for compute-intensive tasks?

exp.a: Incorrect – T-series is general purpose with burstable performance.
exp.b: Incorrect – M-series is general purpose.
exp.c: Correct – C-series (Compute Optimized) is designed for compute-intensive workloads like batch processing, gaming servers.
exp.d: Incorrect – R-series is memory optimized.

q: Which EC2 instance family is best for high-performance databases requiring fast storage?

exp.a: Incorrect – T-series is general purpose.
exp.b: Correct – I-series (Storage Optimized) instances provide high sequential read/write access and NVMe storage for databases.
exp.c: Incorrect – C-series is compute optimized.
exp.d: Incorrect – A-series is ARM-based general purpose.

q: What does the 'T' in T3 instance type represent?

exp.a: Incorrect – T stands for burstable general purpose.
exp.b: Incorrect – T does not stand for Turbo.
exp.c: Correct – T-series instances are burstable general purpose instances that earn CPU credits when idle.
exp.d: Incorrect – T does not stand for Temporal.

q: What happens when a T-series instance exhausts its CPU credits?

opts.b: The instance performance is throttled to baseline

exp.a: Incorrect – The instance is not terminated.
exp.b: Correct – When CPU credits are exhausted, the instance performance is capped at the baseline level (unless unlimited mode is enabled).
exp.c: Incorrect – The instance continues running but at reduced performance.
exp.d: Incorrect – Additional charges only apply if 'unlimited' mode is enabled.

q: Which feature allows you to hibernate an EC2 instance?

exp.a: Incorrect – Stopping an instance does not preserve RAM contents.
exp.b: Correct – EC2 Hibernate saves the contents of RAM to the EBS root volume and resumes the instance to its previous state.
exp.c: Incorrect – 'Suspend' is not an official EC2 feature name.
exp.d: Incorrect – 'Freeze' is not an EC2 feature.

q: What is the maximum RAM size supported for EC2 Hibernate?

exp.a: Incorrect – The limit is higher than 16 GB.
exp.b: Incorrect – The limit is higher than 64 GB.
exp.c: Correct – EC2 Hibernate supports instances with up to 150 GB of RAM.
exp.d: Incorrect – 256 GB exceeds the hibernate limit.

q: What is the maximum duration an EC2 instance can be in hibernation?

exp.a: Incorrect – The limit is much longer than 24 hours.
exp.b: Incorrect – The limit is more than 48 hours.
exp.c: Correct – An EC2 instance can remain in hibernation for up to 60 days.
exp.d: Incorrect – There is a 60-day limit.

q: Which service provides metadata information about a running EC2 instance?

exp.a: Incorrect – CloudTrail logs API calls, not instance metadata.
exp.b: Correct – IMDS provides metadata about the instance (instance ID, IP, IAM role, etc.) accessible at http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/.
exp.c: Incorrect – AWS Config tracks resource configurations.
exp.d: Incorrect – Inspector is for security assessments.

q: What is the IP address used to access EC2 instance metadata?

exp.a: Incorrect – This is a private IP range, not for metadata.
exp.b: Incorrect – This is a VPC default IP, not for metadata.
exp.c: Correct – EC2 instance metadata is accessed at http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/.
exp.d: Incorrect – This is a private IP range.

q: What is an Elastic Network Interface (ENI)?

opts.b: A virtual network interface that can be attached to EC2 instances

exp.a: Incorrect – ENI is virtual, not physical.
exp.b: Correct – An ENI is a virtual network interface that you can attach/detach from EC2 instances within a VPC.
exp.c: Incorrect – ENI is not a DNS resolver.
exp.d: Incorrect – ENI is not a VPN endpoint.

q: Which feature allows you to use your own IP address range in AWS?

exp.a: Incorrect – Elastic IP is an AWS-provided static IP.
exp.b: Correct – BYOIP allows you to bring your own public IPv4 or IPv6 address range into AWS.
exp.c: Incorrect – NAT Gateway enables outbound internet for private subnets.
exp.d: Incorrect – Internet Gateway connects VPC to the internet.

q: What happens to the public IP of an EC2 instance when it is stopped and started?

opts.c: The instance loses internet access permanently

exp.a: Incorrect – The auto-assigned public IP changes on stop/start.
exp.b: Correct – When you stop and start an EC2 instance, the public IPv4 address changes. Use Elastic IP for a static address.
exp.c: Incorrect – It gets a new public IP when restarted.
exp.d: Incorrect – It does not automatically become an Elastic IP.

q: What is the charge for an Elastic IP address that is associated with a running EC2 instance?

exp.a: Incorrect – You are charged when the EIP is NOT associated with a running instance.
exp.b: Correct – An Elastic IP associated with a running instance is free. You are charged when it is not associated or when you have more than one EIP per instance.
exp.c: Incorrect – No charge when associated with a running instance.
exp.d: Incorrect – No charge when in use.

q: Which AWS service provides a managed NFS file system that can be mounted on multiple EC2 instances?

exp.a: Incorrect – EBS can only be attached to one instance at a time (except Multi-Attach io1/io2).
exp.b: Incorrect – S3 is object storage, not a mountable file system.
exp.c: Correct – Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) is a managed NFS that can be mounted on multiple EC2 instances simultaneously.
exp.d: Incorrect – FSx is for Windows File Server or Lustre, not NFS by default.

q: Can an EBS volume be attached to multiple EC2 instances simultaneously?

opts.a: Yes, all EBS types support this
opts.c: Yes, but only io1/io2 with Multi-Attach in the same AZ

exp.a: Incorrect – Only io1/io2 volumes support Multi-Attach.
exp.b: Incorrect – io1/io2 volumes support Multi-Attach.
exp.c: Correct – EBS Multi-Attach allows io1/io2 volumes to be attached to up to 16 instances in the same AZ.
exp.d: Incorrect – Multi-Attach works only within the same AZ.

q: What is the maximum number of instances you can attach to an EBS io1/io2 volume using Multi-Attach?

exp.a: Incorrect – The limit is 16.
exp.b: Incorrect – The limit is 16.
exp.c: Correct – EBS Multi-Attach supports up to 16 Nitro-based instances in the same AZ.
exp.d: Incorrect – 32 exceeds the limit.

q: Which of the following is true about EBS Snapshots?

opts.d: They are stored in Glacier only

exp.a: Incorrect – Snapshots are not stored in EBS.
exp.b: Correct – EBS Snapshots are stored in Amazon S3 (managed by AWS, not in your S3 bucket).
exp.c: Incorrect – Snapshots are not stored in EFS.
exp.d: Incorrect – By default they are stored in S3, though you can archive them to a cheaper tier.

q: Can you create an AMI from a running EC2 instance?

opts.a: No, the instance must be stopped first
opts.b: Yes, you can create an AMI from a running instance
opts.d: Only for instances with instance store

exp.a: Incorrect – You can create an AMI while the instance is running, though stopping is recommended for data consistency.
exp.b: Correct – You can create an AMI from a running instance. AWS will create snapshots of the attached EBS volumes.
exp.c: Incorrect – It works for both Linux and Windows.
exp.d: Incorrect – It works for both EBS-backed and instance store instances.

q: What is the purpose of an EC2 Launch Template?

opts.b: To define instance configuration parameters for launching EC2 instances

exp.a: Incorrect – IAM policies are created in IAM.
exp.b: Correct – Launch Templates define instance configuration (AMI, instance type, key pair, security groups, etc.) and can be used with Auto Scaling.
exp.c: Incorrect – VPC settings are configured separately.
exp.d: Incorrect – Billing alarms are set up in CloudWatch.

q: Which AWS service monitors EC2 instance metrics like CPU utilization by default?

exp.a: Incorrect – CloudTrail monitors API activity.
exp.b: Correct – Amazon CloudWatch monitors EC2 metrics like CPU utilization, network I/O, disk I/O by default.
exp.c: Incorrect – AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes.
exp.d: Incorrect – X-Ray is for distributed tracing.

q: What is the default monitoring interval for EC2 instances in CloudWatch?

exp.a: Incorrect – 1-minute interval requires detailed monitoring (additional cost).
exp.b: Correct – Basic monitoring provides metrics at 5-minute intervals by default.
exp.c: Incorrect – 10 minutes is not a standard interval.
exp.d: Incorrect – 15 minutes is not a standard interval.

q: Which EC2 metric is NOT available in CloudWatch by default and requires a CloudWatch Agent?

exp.a: Incorrect – CPU Utilization is available by default.
exp.b: Correct – Memory utilization is NOT available by default. You need to install the CloudWatch Agent to collect memory and disk-level metrics.
exp.c: Incorrect – Network In/Out is available by default.
exp.d: Incorrect – Disk Read/Write operations are available by default.

q: What is a Dedicated Host in AWS EC2?

opts.b: A physical server fully dedicated to your use
opts.c: A virtual machine with higher CPU

exp.a: Incorrect – A Dedicated Host is not shared.
exp.b: Correct – A Dedicated Host is a physical server with EC2 capacity fully dedicated to your use, useful for compliance and licensing.
exp.c: Incorrect – It is a physical server, not just a VM.
exp.d: Incorrect – It has nothing to do with Spot Instances.

q: What is the difference between a Dedicated Host and a Dedicated Instance?

opts.a: No difference; they are the same
opts.b: Dedicated Host gives visibility into sockets/cores; Dedicated Instance does not
opts.d: Dedicated Host does not support Windows

exp.a: Incorrect – They are different.
exp.b: Correct – Dedicated Host provides visibility into physical server (sockets, cores, host ID) for license compliance. Dedicated Instance just ensures hardware isolation.
exp.c: Incorrect – Dedicated Host is typically more expensive.
exp.d: Incorrect – Dedicated Host supports Windows.

q: Which EC2 feature allows you to assign an IAM role to an instance for accessing other AWS services?

exp.a: Incorrect – Security Groups control network traffic.
exp.b: Correct – An Instance Profile is a container for an IAM role that you attach to an EC2 instance to grant it permissions.
exp.c: Incorrect – Key Pairs are for SSH authentication.
exp.d: Incorrect – User Data is for bootstrapping scripts.

q: What is the SLA uptime commitment for Amazon EC2?

exp.a: Incorrect – EC2 SLA is higher than 99%.
exp.b: Incorrect – EC2 SLA is higher than 99.9%.
exp.c: Incorrect – EC2 SLA is 99.99%.
exp.d: Correct – Amazon EC2 has a 99.99% SLA for each region.

q: Which of the following is a valid Reserved Instance payment option?

opts.a: All Upfront, Partial Upfront, No Upfront

exp.a: Correct – Reserved Instances offer three payment options: All Upfront (highest discount), Partial Upfront, and No Upfront (lowest discount).
exp.b: Incorrect – These are not valid RI payment options.
exp.c: Incorrect – Pay-as-you-go is On-Demand pricing.
exp.d: Incorrect – Credit-based payment is not a valid option.

q: What is EC2 Fleet?

opts.b: A feature that lets you launch a mix of On-Demand, Reserved, and Spot instances in a single request

exp.a: Incorrect – EC2 Fleet is not limited to reserved instances.
exp.b: Correct – EC2 Fleet allows you to launch a combination of On-Demand and Spot instances across multiple instance types in a single API call.
exp.c: Incorrect – EC2 Fleet is not a load balancer.
exp.d: Incorrect – EC2 Fleet is not a placement group.
